name: TAJIKISTAN

flag.title: Tajikistan
flag.note: Tricolour: red, white, green + crown & stars

lead: About 90% of Tajikistan is peaks and valleys. The Pamir Mountains are called the Roof of the World. Half the country sits above 3,000 m.
geo: Ismoil Somoni Peak, at 7,495 m, is the tallest summit of the former Soviet Union. That was a huge Russia-led state. The Fedchenko Glacier, a river of ice, is 77 km long. It is the longest outside the polar regions.
The Nurek Dam is 300 m tall, one of the world's highest. Its 70 km lake fills a canyon and glows bright blue.
animals: The snow leopard is a ghostly grey spotted cat. About 250–280 live in the high Pamirs, hunting ibex (wild goats) and wild sheep.
The Marco Polo sheep is the national animal. Its curly horns can grow over 1.5 m long, the longest of any wild sheep.
culture: Tajiks never turn a guest away. Tea, flatbread (non), and dried fruit cover the dastarkhan, a spread-cloth. Osh, the national dish, is rice with lamb and carrots.
On 21 March, Tajiks celebrate Navruz, the Persian New Year. Cooks stir a sweet porridge, sumalak, all night. People wear bright atlas silk dresses and embroidered skullcaps called tubeteika.
history: Sogdian traders, an ancient Central Asian people, carried silk and gold along these passes for over a thousand years. The Samanid Empire (a Persian kingdom) made Bukhara city a centre of Persian poetry and science.
Russia took the region in the 1800s. Tajikistan became a Soviet republic in 1929. It became independent on 9 September 1991. A civil war ended in 1997.
wows: Dushanbe, the capital, means 'Monday' in Tajik, after a Monday market.
In 2011, Dushanbe's 165 m flagpole was briefly the world's tallest.
The 77 km Fedchenko Glacier is the longest outside the polar regions.
Lake Iskanderkul is named after King Alexander the Great, who legend says drowned his horse there.
A 12-metre sleeping Buddha was found buried in northern Tajikistan in 1966.
Over 93% of Tajikistan is mountains, one of Earth's most rugged countries.
The Nurek Dam is 300 m tall, one of the highest ever built.

myths.fact: Travellers have driven the Pamir Highway for decades. The hard part is distance, not getting in.
Valley summers reach 30 °C. Dushanbe is warm from May to October.
